column1: # tests/absence-rule-census.tsv — every absence rule in tests/test-lib.sh, and
# every function the absence detector flags that is not one. Read by hand.
#   PROVED   shown able to fail by rows in ABSENCE_RULES: it passes an untouched
#            copy of the tree, and fails a stripped one and a planted one
#   PENDING  an absence rule nothing has yet shown able to fail — the debt,
#            ordered below by what a silent lapse would let through
#   NOT      flagged by tests/absence-candidates.awk; a reader found it is not
#            an absence rule, and says what it is instead
# Made on 2026-09-14 from three readings of function bodies: a full audit of the
# suite's absence rules (113 named, 5 later judged not to be), then a
# reading of every other function the detector flagged, twice as it was widened.
# Moving a row to PROVED means adding its rows to ABSENCE_RULES and lowering
# ABSENCE_PENDING in tests/test-lib.sh, in the same change.
# THE ORDER FOR THE PENDING RULES, by what a silent lapse would let through.
# Placed on 2026-09-14 by one reading of each rule's body: what regression it
# catches, and what that would cost somebody using this. (?) marks a placement
# the reader was unsure of. Work a tier to completion before the next, top
# first. A rule leaves this list in the same change that moves its row to
# PROVED; absence_order_covers_every_pending_row holds the list to the rows,
# and each tier's count to the names under it.
#   a port past loopback, the inbound guard weakened, the suite writing the
#   real machine, or data leaving the box
#   work or data destroyed, or silently not kept
#         an agent stop/gc path runs docker rm -f on a sandbox without
#         agent_preserve_workspace; the agent's work is deleted
#         the read-only 'lca agent --live' viewer gains docker rm/kill/stop or
#         POST; watching a run can end it
#         backup.sh/restore.sh drop LCA_MAY_PROMPT=true: a sudoer's backup
#         silently omits chat history, found out at restore
#         (?) a docker probe hardwires strict root, so opted-in backups still
#         skip volumes; or LCA_MAY_PROMPT defaults true
#         (?) update/install/do-user-data replace themselves mid-run and bash
#         executes new text at a stale offset, as root
#         .env, logs, locks or pid files get committed; a git update
#         overwrites a user's .env or ships stale state
#         (?) pkill -f/pgrep -f in code or docs matches the calling shell:
#         kills the user's session or finds a phantom server
#   a report, a verdict or a gate saying fine when it is not; a false green
#         (?) a hand-copied guard-coverage matcher in check-system/apply
#         drifts, reporting ports 3000/3001 guarded when they are not
#         a setting baked into the chat container (e.g. signup) is never
#         drift-compared; .env edits unapplied, status says clean
#         webui_drift reports a key webui.sh has no sentence for; 'lca webui
#         status' falls through to the healthy line
#         ss/ps/docker ps piped into grep -q: SIGPIPE 141 reads a present
#         printf of a big variable into head/grep -q SIGPIPEs above 64KiB;
#         product checks read found as not-found
#         a command-less 'exec 2>/dev/null' silences stderr for the rest of
#         setup.sh hardcodes its finish line instead of setup_verdict;
#         installer can declare success decoupled from step failures
#         selftest.sh prints a hardcoded 'SELF-TEST PASSED' instead of
#         setup passes check-system --quick without a real generation; install
#         verdict skips proving the model answers
#         agent settings POST accepted-and-ignored still prints 'settings
#         seeded'; agent runs with wrong model and ends empty
#         watcher blocks on a silent agent so the wall clock never fires, or
#         'lca check'/'lca test' claim the assistant prompt matches when the
#         a scripts/install_*.sh is never invoked by setup.sh, yet setup
#         completes as if that component were installed
#         lca apply compares ollama ps's live allocation, not the configured
#         context; a setting change is judged already applied
#         a lib function called from if/&&: its failed as_root/rm/docker/tar
#         step is ignored and it returns success
#         a script calls a helper defined in a file it doesn't source; 127
#         inside a condition reads as false
#         check-system's own df rounds up on the wrong filesystem; passes free
#         free-disk lines name an unchecked MODELS_DIR guess; the report
#         describes a filesystem models don't live on
#         (?) a script hand-reads the Ollama drop-in to judge drift; its
#         (?) identification gives up under 120s: user told task NOT submitted
#         while its sandbox starts and runs unwatched
#         (?) stop_followers signals its own process group on exit, killing
#         the watcher before its final run report prints
#         a gate's literal survives only in a comment; the gate passes after
#         the code it guards is deleted
#         a gate greps the file defining a function for its name; passes with
#         a bash -c gate calls lib.sh functions without sourcing; command-not-
#         found turns a negated assertion into a pass
#         a suite '${var} | grep -q' SIGPIPEs under pipefail; gates read a
#         a suite 'sed ... | awk' whose awk exits early kills the writer; the
#         a tracked bash script falls outside Makefile SCRIPTS; syntax errors
#         a new root .md is read by no prose gate and not exempted; every doc
#         a new bin/lca dispatch target has no --help test; its --help could
#         a switch recorded as driven at BOTH values was only ever run at one;
#         the untested path counts as covered
#         a new true/false switch in .env.example gets no coverage row; nobody
#         decides whether its other value is tested
#         SHIPPED-ONLY switches (other value never driven) grow back past zero
#         count of weak source-grep (Group A) gates climbs past 74 unnoticed
#         source-grep census keeps rows for deleted gates, unknown labels or
#   a command, path, flag or port that does not exist or does the wrong
#   thing. Hangs and loud install failures fit no tier and sit at the top of
#         a login-banner curl loses --max-time; on a host without timeout(1)
#         an unbounded docker info/ps/inspect: a daemon that accepts and never
#         answers hangs lca check, webui status
#         (?) a lib helper calls can_root itself, so reporters and the login
#         banner stall waiting for a sudo password
#         (?) a sourced script sets LCA_MAY_PROMPT=true at top level, turning
#         its sourcing reporter into a password prompt
#         (?) select_docker/run_reader open an interactive sudo prompt before
#         trying sudo -n, or without saying why
#         (?) an 'as_root docker info' probe without can_root/root_for_probe
#         a bare rm on a root-owned path aborts uninstall; later units,
#         models, link are left and restart at boot
#         messages/docs offer docker/webui restart to apply a setting;
#         container keeps old baked env, change silently not applied
#         docs tell readers to rerun an install_*.sh after editing .env
#         messages in lca-dispatched scripts pair a .env edit with rerunning
#         a drift warning in check-system/webui omits 'lca apply', leaving no
#         FAQ again promises offline mode physically cannot reach the
#         an offline-mode box is told 'ollama pull' with no mention the kill
#         'lca model X' downloads gigabytes before model_fits_ram rejects the
#         --list-recommended lists models under 'fit this machine' that
#         PERFORMANCE.md calls a model comfortable at a VRAM size where
#         check-system keeps its own RAM staircase and recommends a model
#         check-system.sh hardcodes a TUNE_MODEL tag, recommending a model the
#         README RAM table gives a model/context that choose_for_ram does not
#         README MODEL_FAMILY table advertises size rungs auto-tune never
#         GPU.md VRAM table promises a largest model that
#         INSTALL/TROUBLESHOOTING pair a RAM size with a context length the
#         a silent model is blamed on RAM by hand instead of the measured
#         .env.example gains a line load_env rejects; a fresh .env copy makes
#         (?) a .env.example key has no load_env default (or reverse); older
#         a .env.example key gains no lib.sh default; a .env predating it runs
#         load_env defaults a key .env.example never shows; a behaviour-
#         README settings table lists a removed key or a wrong default;
#         a numeric .env setting goes unvalidated by check-system; a typo
#         a host without systemd is told 'systemctl start docker', or messages
#         no-systemd hosts told journalctl -u ollama / systemctl restart
#         ollama, commands that cannot work there
#         user who cannot reach a healthy daemon told to start it or join the
#         an agent-setup 'blocked' stop names no command to run next
#         apt failure blamed on the dpkg lock or network when sudo could not
#         a message advises running setup.sh or an install_*.sh without sudo;
#         messages or usage say ./x.sh, scripts/x.sh or bare x.sh, which only
#         doc code blocks run ./script.sh without a cd, or prose says run x.sh
#         a message sends the reader to ${SCRIPT_DIR}/${REPO_ROOT} path that
#         docs or messages advise 'x.sh --flag' that the script's help doesn't
#         advice sends users to the internal --install-service flag
#         'lca help' advertises a subcommand bin/lca does not dispatch
#         the model's system prompt names an lca subcommand that doesn't
#         a message points at docs/X.md (section) that doesn't exist or is
#         a script names a .md file absent from repo root, docs/ or config/
#         a tracked doc links to a missing file or #anchor
#         a script calls wait_for_webui directly; a stopped container is
#         'lca speed' reports a cached prompt-read rate, overstating reading
#         a script prints ollama ps placement raw; a CPU-only box is shown a
#         jq '//' turns stored native_tool_calling=false into the default;
#         backups search runs before a readability check; an unreadable
#         backups dir is reported as no backups
#         a message tells users to run ps | grep, which always matches itself;
#         docs glob several backup archives into one tar command, which fails
#         docs scp a remote backup-*.tar.gz glob, copying every retained
#         README names a different open-webui tag than lib.sh pulls, or
#         setup/update/docs chmod different directories; bin/lca or scripts
#         (?) a non-core setup step runs bare; its failure aborts the whole
#         (?) an installer with a SKIP_/ENABLE_ switch runs untested in setup;
#         (?) curl | sh vendor installer has no retry loop; one network blip
#         a script calls set_env_var directly; a failed .env write exits or
#         the login banner can print a state TROUBLESHOOTING.md never explains
#         a .env key shares a name with an aider env var; aider silently picks
#         install_git/check-system read git config themselves; under sudo
#         root's identity is reported, not the user's
#         a script hand-writes SUDO_USER:-$(id -un); wrong account named,
#         chowned or added to docker group
#         a retention sentence prints raw BACKUP_KEEP instead of
#         retention_desc, misdescribing how many backups are kept
#         a doc teaches a 'cd ... && lca' handover recipe the system prompt no
#         a script prints a 'my-project && ' recipe that differs from the
#         lca ask writes info/ok/step lines to stdout, corrupting an answer
#         ensure_ollama_up >/dev/null: up to 60s of silence while Ollama
#         bin/lca dispatches a subcommand 'lca help' never mentions
#         update-model.sh accepts a flag 'lca help' never mentions
#         a command in 'lca help' is missing from the README command table
#         README/CONTRIBUTING/pre-push state the wrong CI job count,
#         understating what a local push leaves unchecked
#         PERFORMANCE.md prose quotes a bold speed that differs from its
#         PERFORMANCE.md presents a second untilded tokens/second figure for a
#   duplication and wording; a lapse costs maintainability, not users
#         (?) the open-webui image literal is written a second time outside
#         .ollama-serve.log is spelled out again instead of OLLAMA_BG_LOG
#         a script builds .venv/bin/python|pip|aider by hand instead of
#         install.sh repeats next-step commands after setup.sh already printed
#         a message recites the '0.6 GB per billion' sizing formula instead of
#         chat start screen ships Open WebUI's stock suggestions (Roman
#         empire, kids' art) instead of coding prompts
#         lib.sh honours an env name that is neither in .env.example nor
#         a failing path prints usage to stdout instead of stderr
#         a scripts/*.sh file is never mentioned in the README
#         CONTRIBUTING.md names functions or files that no longer exist
#         Makefile header lists make targets that don't exist, or omits real
#         a CONTRIBUTING.md heading's stated count ('Eleven ...') disagrees
#         source-grep census's published work order misses or duplicates Group
#         a tracked path starting with '-' or containing whitespace, misparsed
